newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST - Italy market puts rate cut hopes on hold.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Italy market puts rate cut hopes on hold.

text.p: Italy's money market has put a brake on expectations for a short term monetary easing, a study by the Bocconi University's Igier research arm showed on Friday.

Many operators had expected the Bank of Italy to cut its 6.75 percent discount rate after preliminary cities' CPI data indicated May inflation falling to 1.5 percent from April's 1.7 percent. Final national May CPI data are due out on June 4.

But now some in the market are starting to fear the widely expected easing will not take place, and according to the Igier study, which is based on implicit forward rates, the scope for a rate cut has been reduced.
And European tensions, from French elections to the German gold reserves row, have complicated the situation even more.

On a one month timeframe, the implicit overnight rate was seen standing at 6.92 percent compared to an actual market close of 6.99 percent on Thursday, the day on which Igier based its study. One week ago, the implicit overnight rate on the same time horizon was seen at 6.78 percent.
On a three month horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen at 6.79 compared with 6.57 percent a week ago and 6.92 percent a month ago.
On a one year horizon, the implicit overnight rate was seen falling to 6.60 percent from 6.35 percent seen a week ago and 6.74 percent seen one month ago.
On a two year timeframe, the falling trend should be reversed with the implicit overnight rate seen at 6.85 percent from 6.80 percent seen a week ago.

The spread between the Italian implicit overnight rate and that in Germany on a two year horizon, considered a good indicator of market confidence of Italy's entry in Europe's economic and monetary union, was seen at 205 basis points, compared with 203 bps seen a week ago and 237 bps a month ago.
